The GP was delayed, however the receptionist did not feel it was necessary to inform the patients that were waiting to see the GP. The reception muttered that she had informed another paient. I am afraid that as a patient I have no idea how many clinicians are working and if a statement that was given to another patient in a conversation at the reception desk. Generally as a patient I would not listen into another patients conversation.

It is basic customer service.....as a receptionist I would hope that matters such as this would be high on your list. I.e keeping patients informed about the situation....it is basic common courtesy.

It is also not necessary to take a defensive stance when speaking with patients, you were asked a simple question....a simple answer would be acceptable.....not a justification of why you did not do something.

For clarity this was an appointment at 2.10 at tile hill 30/12.

It is totally acceptable that a clinician may be delayed.....most patients will be fine with that as long as they are kept informed.

This was a clear failure at the reception desk, with a receptionist that did not think it was necessary to inform the patient or indeed make any effort to apologise for her oversite or defensive attitude.

I will be logging a formal complaint with the actual obdnusman if I do not. Get a satisfactory reply. I’m truley appalled at the service and lack of empathy. I’m sure I am not the only patient to have lost their medication twice in over 10 years.
oh and 1 of the doctors. There was always something annoying with the appointments and all the interactions. The reception first of all are so impolite and very aggressive. Coventry is a multi national city and not everyone knows about the NHS routes and routines, most of the times the question were taken with some kind of aggression and the term "you should know". Its not easy to get appointments and we never managed to get an emergency one the same day. I realised the difference in the low quality of booking appointments when I changed my surgery to the address of the new home. Also the telephone lines are so busy and never you are picked up sooner than half an hour or so.
There are a lots of GPs in this surgery and definitely not all of them are recommendable. We were super happy with Dr Wiggins and Newbold who were always there to listen and help kindly. We never felt cared by others such as Dr Kumar.
The nursing is good though, there are kind and listening. During pregnancy the care was alright, except that each time I was visited by a different midwife.
